 EXCLUSIVE: Biodance, Medicube Open Counters at Selfridges’ New K-beauty Destination, The Beauty Workshop
 WWD Follow Samantha Conti Mon, November 2, 2026 at 5:01 AM UTC Add to Preferred Sources Mon, November 2, 2026 at 5:01 AM UTC LONDON — The K-beauty colossus is landing at Selfridges .
 U.K. beauty distributor Luneia Brands has partnered with the department store to launch two counters for Biodance and Medicube that will anchor a wider destination for K-beauty at the Oxford Street flagship.
 More from WWD

 Advertisement Advertisement The openings, on Monday, signal a shift in strategy from social media to physical retail. The Biodance counter will be its first permanent one worldwide, while the Medicube unit will be its first in Europe. It is also the first time the two Korean skin care brands will launch permanent counters together.
 Both counters will be housed in Selfridges ' new K-beauty destination, The Beauty Workshop. Other brands in The Beauty Workshop include Beauty of Joseon, Thank You Farmer, Skin1004, Axis-Y, VT Cosmetics and Dr. Reju-All.
 According to Luneia, the launch signals a new chapter for Korean beauty within luxury retail, moving beyond viral trends toward permanent, immersive spaces that are focused on innovation, education and personalized skin care.
 Biodance and Medicube are two of the biggest players in Korean skin care. According to parent company APR, Medicube's Age-R beauty devices have surpassed 6 million global sales, while Biodance has sold more than 350 million hydrogel masks worldwide.
 Advertisement Advertisement Both Selfridges counters have been designed as immersive spaces "for discovery and education," and will showcase both brands' most extensive physical product ranges.
 The counters will offer visual merchandising, hands-on demonstrations and personalized consultations, including bespoke skin care advice, exclusives and preview launches. Further first-to-market innovations are planned throughout 2027.
 Medicube will also introduce a dedicated facial devices bar, giving customers the opportunity to explore and trial its Age-R beauty technology, including the bestselling Age-R Booster Pro, alongside the wider skin care portfolio.
 Biodance will mark its Selfridges launch with activations and gifting experiences throughout November. It will introduce a launch-day Lucky Dip and limited-edition beauty goody bags, while Medicube will partner with Selfridges' Elevate smoothie bar to offer complimentary branded smoothies with qualifying purchases.
 Medicube is opening a permanent space at Selfridges' beauty hall.
 Gemma Murari, managing director of Luneia Brands, said the launch of both brands "signals how much the Korean beauty market continues to mature and evolve."
 Advertisement Advertisement She added Luneia Brands worked closely with Selfridges to bring the vision to life, "and set a new standard for how K-beauty is presented, not only in the U.K. but on a global stage."
 As K-beauty gains momentum worldwide it has begun raising its game, changing its distribution model, and shifting from social marketing and sales to physical spaces.
 Murari said the category "has outgrown the way it has traditionally been sold. It was built on viral moments, and it scaled through social commerce and wide, fast distribution. That has created extraordinary awareness, but it has left the customer without a place to go deeper. Today's K-beauty shopper is highly educated, ingredient-literate and is looking for expertise, discovery and a reason to shop in person."
 She added: "We believe K-beauty is not a bubble, but a maturing category. The leading brands are becoming established household names with appeal across generations."
 Advertisement Advertisement Jade Mainprize, beauty buyer at Selfridges, said Korean brands have begun approaching international retail differently, and "our ambition is to build long-term partnerships with these brands and play a role in establishing their longevity in the U.K. market. We want to help nurture them into the next generation of household names."
 She added that Selfridges' K-beauty destination is central to the store's vision, and "goes beyond discovery. It's about building confidence, credibility and lasting relationships with our customers, while championing the innovation and expertise at the heart of Korean beauty."
